transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what's been bothering you or what brings you in today?

I came in because… I don’t know, for the past few weeks I’ve just had this really heavy sadness on me. It’s like this pressure sitting in my chest or over me all day, and I can’t really shake it. Even when I’m at work and I’m doing what I’m supposed to do—smiling at patients, talking to people, trying to seem normal—I feel like inside I’m barely keeping it together. It’s exhausting pretending I’m okay when I feel so low most of the day.
Have you noticed that you’re not enjoying things as much as you used to, even activities you normally like?

Yeah… definitely. That’s actually been one of the things that scared me, because I used to have things I genuinely looked forward to after my shifts. Like, even if work was draining, I’d come home and paint for a while, or I’d go to yoga, or sometimes salsa if I had the energy, and it helped me feel like I was still a person outside of work.

But lately I just… don’t. I get home and I sit on the couch, and I’ll think, “I should paint,” or “I should go to class,” and then it feels like this huge amount of effort for something that doesn’t even sound enjoyable anymore. And people text me about plans or checking in, and I just ignore it because answering feels like too much, and also I don’t really feel like I have anything to say. None of it feels worth it right now.
Have you been feeling like you’re not good enough or blaming yourself for things more than usual?

I’m… not really sure. I mean, I don’t think I’ve been walking around thinking “I’m a terrible person” or anything that clear. It’s more like… I know I’m not myself, and I get frustrated with that, but I don’t know if I’d call it blaming myself exactly.

Sometimes I’ll wonder why I can’t just snap out of it or do the things I normally do, and then I feel kind of embarrassed about being like this, especially because I’m usually pretty functional and people rely on me. But I don’t know… I haven’t noticed a big constant thing of feeling worthless, if that’s what you mean. It’s more confusion and feeling stuck than blaming myself for specific things.
Have you been feeling more tired or lacking energy lately, even when you’re not doing much physically?

I’m not sure how to answer that, honestly. I mean… I feel worn down, but I don’t know if it’s “tired” in the physical sense, like if I’d been running around all day or not sleeping enough. It’s more like everything feels heavier to start, if that makes sense.

But I haven’t really been tracking my energy in a clear way. Some days I can still get through what I need to do, and other times I just kind of sit there and feel like I don’t have much in me. I don’t know if that’s the same as lacking energy, or if it’s just the sadness making everything feel harder.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight lately—like eating a lot less or more than usual, or losing or gaining weight without trying?

Yeah… I think so. I haven’t really weighed myself consistently, so I can’t say for sure about the number, but my appetite is definitely off.

It’s like I know, logically, that I should be eating regular meals—especially with my job, because I’m on my feet and I know better—but food just sounds… unappealing most of the time. Not nauseating exactly, just like nothing sounds worth making or eating. I’ll tell myself I’ll eat something before I leave, and then I don’t, or I’ll pack something and it just sits there.

There have been days where I’m halfway through a clinic shift and suddenly realize all I’ve had is coffee, or maybe some crackers from my bag, and I didn’t even really notice until I started feeling kind of empty. It’s not intentional, like I’m not trying to diet or anything. I just don’t feel hungry in the normal way, and making a real meal feels like this whole task I don’t want to deal with.
Have you been having trouble sleeping lately—like waking up in the middle of the night, not being able to fall asleep, or sleeping much more than usual even when you don’t feel tired?

I don’t really know. I mean, I haven’t been paying close attention to my sleep in a way where I could tell you a clear pattern, like “I wake up at 3 a.m. every night” or anything like that.

Some nights I go to bed and I feel like I’m just… lying there with my eyes closed for a while, but I don’t know if it’s actually a long time or if it just feels long because I’m aware of it. And then other nights I think I sleep okay enough, or at least I don’t remember anything dramatic happening. I haven’t noticed that I’m suddenly sleeping all day or anything like that.

I guess the honest answer is that sleep hasn’t stood out to me as the main thing. I feel off, but I can’t say confidently that it’s because I’m not sleeping or that my sleep has changed in some specific way.
Have you felt down or depressed most of the day, nearly every day, for at least the past two weeks?

Yes… yeah, I think that’s actually the main reason I came in. For the past few weeks it’s been this heavy, sad feeling that’s just kind of sitting on me most of the day. It’s not like I’m crying constantly or anything, but it’s there almost all the time, like pressure in my chest or in the background of everything I’m doing.

And I can still function outwardly, sort of. Like at work, I’ll smile at patients and say the right things and try to sound normal, because that’s what you do, and I don’t want to bring that into their care. But inside I feel like I’m barely keeping it together. It’s exhausting trying to look okay when I really don’t feel okay.

So… yes, most days, most of the day. It’s been hard to shake.
Have you noticed that you've been moving or speaking more slowly than usual, or have you felt physically slowed down or restless nearly every day?

Yes… slowed down, definitely. Not so much restless, at least that’s not the part I notice. It’s more like everything takes this ridiculous amount of effort, like I’m moving through syrup or something.

At the clinic, it’s been really obvious to me, which is embarrassing because I’m usually pretty efficient. Like if I need to gather supplies for a dressing change, I’ll know exactly what I need, but my body just doesn’t move with any urgency. I’m walking slower, reaching for things slower, double-checking myself more slowly. Even charting, which I can normally get through pretty quickly, feels like it takes forever. I’ll be sitting there trying to finish a note and it’s like my hands and my brain are both lagging.

I don’t think I’m doing it on purpose, and I don’t always realize it right away. But then I look at the time and think, “Why did that take me so long?” Simple things just feel… heavier than they should.
Have you had episodes like this before, where you felt down or lost interest in things for a period of time?

I’m not really sure how to answer that cleanly. I mean… I’ve had bad weeks before, like anyone has, where I was stressed or kind of shut down for a bit. But I don’t know if I’d call them episodes like this.

I don’t remember having a stretch that felt this heavy or this hard to shake, at least not in a way where I thought, “This is something I should probably talk to someone about.” Maybe there were times I felt low, but I can’t clearly say it was the same thing or that it lasted a certain amount of time.

So… I guess my answer is I’m not sure. Nothing stands out to me as clearly as what’s been happening lately.
Have you ever had a period in the past where you felt down or lost interest in things for at least two weeks, similar to what you’ve been experiencing lately?

I don’t think so… not in a way I can clearly identify, at least.

I mean, I’ve definitely had times where I felt low or overwhelmed, or where I wasn’t as excited about things as I usually would be. But when you say at least two weeks and similar to this, I’m trying to really think back, and nothing comes to mind that feels like the same thing. Not this kind of heaviness that lasts day after day and feels hard to climb out of.

So I guess… no clear past episode that I can point to. I don’t want to say it never happened with absolute certainty, because memory is kind of messy, but I don’t remember anything like what I’ve been dealing with lately.
Can you think back and confirm if there has ever been a time before this current period where you felt down or lost interest in things for two weeks or more?

I can’t really confirm that, no. I’ve been trying to think about it, because I don’t want to give you the wrong answer just because my memory is fuzzy, but nothing clear comes up.

Like, I’ve had rough patches before, sure — times where I was stressed, or tired of everything, or just kind of emotionally checked out for a while. But when you’re asking specifically about two weeks or more of feeling down or losing interest in things the way it’s been happening now… I don’t remember a definite period like that.

So I guess the most honest answer is: not that I can identify. I don’t think there’s been a previous time that clearly fits that.
Can you think back and confirm if there has ever been a time before this current period where you felt down or lost interest in things for two weeks or more?

I still can’t really confirm it, no. I know I’ve kind of answered that already, but I keep turning it over in my head because the “two weeks or more” part makes me second-guess myself.

There have been times before where I wasn’t doing great, where I felt drained or not like myself for a while, but I don’t have a clear memory of a past stretch that was like this and lasted that long. Nothing where I can honestly say, yes, that was definitely the same kind of thing for two weeks or more.

So I guess the most accurate answer is… I don’t think so, or at least not that I can clearly identify. I wouldn’t want to say an absolute “never,” because I’m not sure my memory is that precise, but no, nothing definite comes to mind before this current period.
